utilityName: City of Oxnard Water Division Backflow Prevention
testingFrequency: Annual certification requirements enforced through web-based Tokay reporting
dueBasis: Oxnard says all approved backflow testing companies and testers are required to submit test results online through web-based backflow test reporting using Tokay software.
coveredPropertyTypes: Oxnard water customers with backflow prevention assemblies
Sites subject to annual certification requirements
coveredDeviceTypes: Devices tested by approved companies or testers
officialListLabel: Open Oxnard Tokay tester credential instructions
penalties: Oxnard says no tests submitted to the City will be accepted without the required tester information, and expired certificates can suspend login credentials until renewed certificates are received.
sourceExcerpt: Oxnard is a strong Tokay WebTest page because the City names Tokay software, requires approved testers to submit online, asks for tester certification and business license information, and suspends credentials when certificates expire.
verdictSummary: Oxnard is a strong Southern California Tokay page because the city moved approved tester report submission into web-based Tokay reporting and ties access to current credentials.
whoIsAffected: Oxnard water customers with required assemblies and approved backflow testing companies or testers submitting annual certification results.
residentialNotes: Residential scope depends on whether the property has a required assembly in Oxnard's program.
Customers should make sure the tester can submit through Oxnard's Tokay workflow.
commercialNotes: Commercial and managed properties should confirm the tester is approved and has active Tokay access before scheduling.
Expired tester credentials can interrupt report acceptance.

annualTesting.summary: Oxnard uses Tokay software to enforce online annual certification reporting.
highlights: Approved testers must submit results online.
Required tester information must be provided before tests are accepted.
Expired certificates can suspend portal login credentials.
workflowSteps: Confirm the assembly is due under Oxnard's annual certification process.
Use an approved tester with current required information on file.
Submit the test result through the Tokay workflow.
Confirm whether the assembly is due under Oxnard's annual certification requirements.
Make sure the tester has provided valid tester information to the City.
Use the Tokay online reporting workflow for the completed test.
Renew expired certificates before expecting login access or report acceptance.
failureHighlights: Oxnard says tests will not be accepted without required tester information.
Online submission is required for approved testers.

costBand.testingRange: Testing is market-priced by approved testers.
costBand.repairRetestRange: Repair and retest costs depend on device type and whether another accepted Tokay entry is required.
costBand.pricingNotes: Oxnard's public friction is credentialed Tokay reporting rather than a published retail test price.
